source.text: מַשָּׂ֥א דְבַר־יְהוָ֖ה עַל־יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל נְאֻם־יְהוָ֗ה נֹטֶ֤ה שָׁמַ֨יִם֙ וְיֹסֵ֣ד אָ֔רֶץ וְיֹצֵ֥ר רֽוּחַ־אָדָ֖ם בְּקִרְבּֽוֹ׃פ

records.literal_gloss: Oracle. [The] word of Yahweh concerning Israel. Declaration of Yahweh, stretching out [the] heavens, and founding [the] earth, and forming [the] spirit of humankind within him:

en.L: An oracle. The word of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} concerning Israel. Declares {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, who stretches out [the] heavens and founds [the] earth and forms the spirit of {{gender:a person|man}} within {{gender:them|him}}:
en.B: An oracle. The word of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} concerning Israel. This is what {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} declares, who stretches out the heavens, lays the foundations of the earth and forms the human spirit within each person:
en.R: This is a message from {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} about Israel. {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} stretched out the sky and laid the foundations of the earth. He gives each person a spirit within them. This is what {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} says:

pt.L: Oráculo: a palavra {{divine_name:do SENHOR|de Javé}} a respeito de Israel. Declara {{divine_name:o SENHOR|Javé}}, que estende [os] céus e funda [a] terra e forma o espírito do {{gender:ser humano|homem}} dentro dele:
pt.B: Mensagem: a palavra {{divine_name:do SENHOR|de Javé}} a respeito de Israel. É isto que declara {{divine_name:o SENHOR|Javé}}, que estende os céus, lança os alicerces da terra e forma o espírito humano dentro de cada pessoa:
pt.R: Esta é uma mensagem {{divine_name:do SENHOR|de Javé}} a respeito de Israel. {{divine_name:O SENHOR|Javé}} estendeu o céu e lançou os alicerces da terra. Ele dá a cada pessoa um espírito dentro dela. É isto que {{deity_pronoun:ele|Ele}} diz:

decisions.choice: oracle ... concerning Israel: the heading of the last part of the book (chapters 12-14)
decisions.reason: The heading repeats 9:1 and begins the second of the two oracles that close the book. Chapters 12-14 speak of a final attack of the nations on Jerusalem, the LORD's rescue of the city, the cleansing of his people and his reign over all the earth. The phrase "on that day" comes again and again. The oracle is about Judah and Jerusalem, but it is headed "concerning Israel": Israel is the name of the whole people of God.

decisions.choice: who stretches out the heavens, founds the earth, forms the human spirit: the Creator speaks
decisions.reason: The LORD who speaks is named by what he has made, as in Isaiah 42:5, 44:24 and 51:13, and Psalm 104:2-5. The one who made heaven and earth and gives every human being life can do what this oracle promises. "Spirit" is the breath of life and the inner self (Genesis 2:7; Isaiah 57:16).

decisions.choice: declares the LORD: here at the start of the oracle
decisions.reason: The formula usually comes in the middle or at the end of a saying. Here it stands at the head of the oracle, joined to the titles of the Creator, as in Numbers 24:3-4 and Psalm 110:1, where the same word introduces a solemn saying.

decisions.choice: An oracle (L, B); a message (R); declares the LORD (L, B); This is what he says (R); the spirit of a person within them (L, gender setting)
decisions.reason: The heading follows 9:1. Readable breaks the Creator's titles into short sentences. The Hebrew "humankind" means men and women, so Literal takes the gender setting; Balanced says "the human spirit within each person", which needs none.

decisions.choice: Oráculo: a palavra do SENHOR (L); Mensagem: (B); Esta é uma mensagem (R)
decisions.reason: The heading keeps the wording of 9:1 at each level (m1), as the English does (r-en-1).

decisions.choice: o espírito do ser humano / do homem dentro dele (one gender span)
alternatives: do ser humano dentro dele ou dela
decisions.reason: The English Literal has two spans, "a person ... them". Portuguese needs only one, on the noun: "dele" agrees with both "ser humano" and "homem", so the pronoun takes no span (docs/portuguese-style.md, section 7).

source.text: הִנֵּ֣ה אָ֠נֹכִי שָׂ֣ם אֶת־יְרוּשָׁלִַ֧ם סַף־רַ֛עַל לְכָל־הָעַמִּ֖ים סָבִ֑יב וְגַ֧ם עַל־יְהוּדָ֛ה יִֽהְיֶ֥ה בַמָּצ֖וֹר עַל־יְרוּשָׁלִָֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: Look, I [am] making Jerusalem a cup of reeling for all the peoples around; and also on Judah it will be in the siege on Jerusalem.

en.L: Look, I am making Jerusalem a cup of reeling for all the peoples around; and Judah also will be in the siege against Jerusalem.
en.B: Look, I am about to make Jerusalem a cup that sends all the surrounding peoples reeling. Judah too will be caught up in the siege against Jerusalem.
en.R: I am going to make Jerusalem like a cup of strong wine that makes all the nations around it stagger like drunk people. When enemies surround Jerusalem and attack it, Judah will be attacked too.

pt.L: Eis que faço de Jerusalém um cálice de atordoamento para todos os povos ao redor; e também Judá estará no cerco contra Jerusalém.
pt.B: Vou fazer de Jerusalém um cálice que fará cambalear todos os povos ao redor. Judá também será envolvida no cerco contra Jerusalém.
pt.R: Vou fazer Jerusalém ficar como um cálice de vinho forte, que faz todas as nações ao redor dela cambalearem como bêbados. Quando os inimigos cercarem Jerusalém e a atacarem, Judá também vai ser atacada.

decisions.choice: a cup of reeling: the cup of God's anger that makes the nations stagger
decisions.reason: The prophets picture God's judgment as a cup of strong wine that those who drink it cannot keep from drinking, and that leaves them staggering (Isaiah 51:17, 22; Jeremiah 25:15-28; Psalm 75:9). The nations who come to drink, that is, to take Jerusalem, will be made drunk and helpless by it.

decisions.choice: Judah also will be in the siege: Judah shares Jerusalem's danger
alternatives: Judah will be made to take part in the siege of Jerusalem
decisions.reason: The Hebrew is brief: "and also on Judah it will be in the siege on Jerusalem". It is read here as saying that the towns of Judah will also be under attack when Jerusalem is besieged. Some read it as saying that Judah will be forced to join the siege against Jerusalem. Verses 5-7 show Judah and Jerusalem on the same side.

decisions.choice: like a cup of strong wine ... stagger like drunk people; When enemies surround Jerusalem and attack it (R)
decisions.reason: Readable explains the cup (m1) and the siege.

decisions.choice: um cálice de atordoamento (L); um cálice que fará cambalear (B, R)
decisions.reason: "Cálice" is the word the prophets' cup of judgment has in Portuguese (m1); "cambalear" says what it does to those who drink it.

source.text: וְהָיָ֣ה בַיּוֹם־הַ֠הוּא אָשִׂ֨ים אֶת־יְרוּשָׁלִַ֜ם אֶ֤בֶן מַֽעֲמָסָה֙ לְכָל־הָ֣עַמִּ֔ים כָּל־עֹמְסֶ֖יהָ שָׂר֣וֹט יִשָּׂרֵ֑טוּ וְנֶאֶסְפ֣וּ עָלֶ֔יהָ כֹּ֖ל גּוֹיֵ֥י הָאָֽרֶץ׃

records.literal_gloss: And it will be on that day [that] I will make Jerusalem a stone of burden for all the peoples; all who lift it will surely injure themselves, and will be gathered against it all [the] nations of the earth.

en.L: And it will be in that day [that] I will set Jerusalem [as] a stone of burden for all the peoples; all who carry it will surely gash themselves; and all the nations of the earth will be gathered against it.
en.B: On that day I will make Jerusalem a heavy stone for all the peoples; everyone who tries to lift it will be badly hurt. And all the nations of the earth will gather against it.
en.R: At that time I will make Jerusalem like a heavy stone for all the nations. Everyone who tries to lift it will be badly hurt. All the nations of the earth will come together to attack it.

pt.L: E acontecerá naquele dia [que] farei de Jerusalém uma pedra pesada para todos os povos; todos os que a carregarem certamente se ferirão; e todas as nações da terra se ajuntarão contra ela.
pt.B: Naquele dia farei de Jerusalém uma pedra pesada para todos os povos; todos os que tentarem levantá-la ficarão gravemente feridos. E todas as nações da terra se reunirão contra ela.
pt.R: Naquele dia vou fazer Jerusalém ficar como uma pedra pesada para todas as nações. Todos os que tentarem levantá-la vão se machucar muito. Todas as nações da terra vão se juntar para atacá-la.

decisions.choice: a heavy stone: a stone too heavy to lift without injury
decisions.reason: The phrase means "a stone of burden", a stone to be lifted and carried. Jerome, writing in the land of Israel in the fourth century AD, says that young men there tested their strength by lifting heavy round stones. The nations who try to carry Jerusalem off will find it too heavy and will hurt themselves.

decisions.choice: will surely gash themselves: be cut and badly hurt
decisions.reason: The verb means to cut or scratch (Leviticus 21:5), and the doubled form makes it strong. Lifting the stone tears the lifter's own flesh.

decisions.choice: And it will be in that day [that] (L); On that day (B); At that time (R)
decisions.reason: The phrase follows the wording set in Isaiah. Literal keeps the Hebrew "and it will be", as in Joel 4:18.

decisions.choice: E acontecerá naquele dia [que] (L); Naquele dia (B, R)
decisions.reason: "Naquele dia" at every level, as set for the whole book at 2:15, where the English Readable says "At that time" (also verses 4, 6, 8, 9, 11 and chapters 13-14); Literal keeps the Hebrew "E acontecerá", as Isaiah 2:2 has it in Portuguese.

source.text: בַּיּ֨וֹם הַה֜וּא נְאֻם־יְהוָ֗ה אַכֶּ֤ה כָל־סוּס֙ בַּתִּמָּה֔וֹן וְרֹכְב֖וֹ בַּשִּׁגָּע֑וֹן וְעַל־בֵּ֤ית יְהוּדָה֙ אֶפְקַ֣ח אֶת־עֵינַ֔י וְכֹל֙ ס֣וּס הָֽעַמִּ֔ים אַכֶּ֖ה בַּֽעִוָּרֽוֹן׃

records.literal_gloss: On that day, declaration of Yahweh, I will strike every horse with panic and its rider with madness; and on [the] house of Judah I will open my eyes, and every horse of the peoples I will strike with blindness.

en.L: In that day, declares {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, I will strike every horse with bewilderment and its rider with madness; but over the house of Judah I will open {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} eyes, and every horse of the peoples I will strike with blindness.
en.B: On that day, declares {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, I will strike all the horses with terror and their riders with madness. I will keep {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} eyes open over the house of Judah, but I will strike the horses of the peoples with blindness.
en.R: At that time, says {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, I will make every horse panic and make its rider go mad. I will watch over the people of Judah, but I will make all the horses of the enemy armies blind.

pt.L: Naquele dia, declara {{divine_name:o SENHOR|Javé}}, ferirei todo cavalo com pânico e o seu cavaleiro com loucura; mas sobre a casa de Judá abrirei os {{deity_pronoun:meus|Meus}} olhos, e todo cavalo dos povos ferirei com cegueira.
pt.B: Naquele dia, declara {{divine_name:o SENHOR|Javé}}, ferirei todos os cavalos com terror e os seus cavaleiros com loucura. Manterei os {{deity_pronoun:meus|Meus}} olhos abertos sobre a casa de Judá, mas ferirei com cegueira os cavalos dos povos.
pt.R: Naquele dia, diz {{divine_name:o SENHOR|Javé}}, vou fazer todos os cavalos entrarem em pânico e os seus cavaleiros ficarem loucos. Vou cuidar do povo de Judá, mas vou deixar cegos todos os cavalos dos exércitos inimigos.

decisions.choice: panic, madness, blindness: the curses of Deuteronomy 28:28 turned on the enemy
decisions.reason: Deuteronomy 28:28 warns that if Israel breaks the covenant, the LORD will strike them "with madness, with blindness and with confusion of heart". The same three words are used here, but now the LORD turns them on the nations who attack his people.

decisions.choice: I will open my eyes over the house of Judah: I will watch over them with care
decisions.reason: To have one's eyes open toward someone is to watch over them and care for them (1 Kings 8:29; Psalm 32:8). The enemy's horses are blinded, but the LORD's eyes are open over his people.

decisions.choice: In that day, declares the LORD (L); On that day, declares the LORD (B); At that time, says the LORD (R)
decisions.reason: The formulas follow the wording set in Isaiah. Readable says "watch over" for "open my eyes" (m2) and "enemy armies" for "the peoples". The LORD speaks of his own eyes, so "my" takes the deity_pronoun setting.

decisions.choice: pânico, loucura, cegueira
decisions.reason: The three curses of Deuteronomy 28:28 (m1) are "loucura", "cegueira" and "pânico", plain Portuguese words a reader can recognise there.

source.text: וְאָֽמְר֛וּ אַלֻּפֵ֥י יְהוּדָ֖ה בְּלִבָּ֑ם אַמְצָ֥ה לִי֙ יֹשְׁבֵ֣י יְרוּשָׁלִַ֔ם בַּיהוָ֥ה צְבָא֖וֹת אֱלֹהֵיהֶֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: And will say [the] clans of Judah in their heart, Strength to me [are the] inhabitants of Jerusalem in Yahweh of hosts their God.

en.L: And Judah's clans will say in their heart, "The inhabitants of Jerusalem [are] strength to me through {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} of hosts, their God."
en.B: Then the clans of Judah will say to themselves, "The people of Jerusalem are our strength, through {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} of Armies, their God."
en.R: Then the family groups of Judah will say to themselves, "The people of Jerusalem give us strength, because {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} of Armies is their God."

pt.L: E os clãs de Judá dirão no seu coração: "Os habitantes de Jerusalém [são] força para mim {{divine_name:no SENHOR|em Javé}} dos Exércitos, o Deus deles."
pt.B: Então os clãs de Judá dirão a si mesmos: "O povo de Jerusalém é a nossa força, por meio {{divine_name:do SENHOR|de Javé}} dos Exércitos, o Deus deles."
pt.R: Então as famílias de Judá vão pensar: "O povo de Jerusalém nos dá força, porque {{divine_name:o SENHOR|Javé}} dos Exércitos é o Deus deles."

decisions.choice: the clans of Judah: Judah's clans and their leaders
decisions.reason: The word is the one used in 9:7, meaning a clan or the chief of a clan. Here it may mean Judah's leaders, who speak for their clans. Either way, the people of the countryside speak.

decisions.choice: the inhabitants of Jerusalem are strength to me through the LORD: Judah takes heart from Jerusalem and its God
alternatives: the inhabitants of Jerusalem have strength in the LORD of hosts their God
decisions.reason: The Hebrew is awkward, and its sense is debated. It is read here as Judah's clans saying that the people of Jerusalem give them strength, because the LORD of hosts is with the city. A small change in the letters gives "there is strength for the inhabitants of Jerusalem in the LORD of hosts their God". Both say that the strength comes from the LORD.

decisions.choice: say in their heart (L); say to themselves (B, R); our strength (B); give us strength (R); the LORD of Armies (B, R)
decisions.reason: "Say in their heart" is the Hebrew way of saying "think". The clans speak as one ("me"); Balanced and Readable say "us".

source.text: בַּיּ֣וֹם הַה֡וּא אָשִׂים֩ אֶת־אַלֻּפֵ֨י יְהוּדָ֜ה כְּֽכִיּ֧וֹר אֵ֣שׁ בְּעֵצִ֗ים וּכְלַפִּ֥יד אֵשׁ֙ בְּעָמִ֔יר וְאָ֨כְל֜וּ עַל־יָמִ֧ין וְעַל־שְׂמֹ֛אול אֶת־כָּל־הָעַמִּ֖ים סָבִ֑יב וְיָשְׁבָ֨ה יְרוּשָׁלִַ֥ם ע֛וֹד תַּחְתֶּ֖יהָ בִּירוּשָׁלִָֽם׃פ

records.literal_gloss: On that day I will make [the] clans of Judah like a pot of fire among wood and like a torch of fire among sheaves, and they will devour on [the] right and on [the] left all the peoples around; and Jerusalem will dwell again in her place, in Jerusalem.

en.L: In that day I will make the clans of Judah like a pot of fire among wood and like a torch of fire among sheaves; and they will devour, on the right and on the left, all the peoples around; and Jerusalem will dwell again in her place, in Jerusalem.
en.B: On that day I will make Judah's clans like a firepot set in a pile of wood, like a flaming torch among sheaves of grain. They will consume all the surrounding peoples on the right and on the left, while Jerusalem stays secure in its place.
en.R: At that time I will make the family groups of Judah like a pot of burning coals in a pile of wood, or like a burning torch among bundles of grain. They will destroy all the nations around them, on every side. But Jerusalem will stay safe where it is.

pt.L: Naquele dia farei os clãs de Judá como um braseiro no meio da lenha e como uma tocha de fogo no meio dos feixes; e devorarão, à direita e à esquerda, todos os povos ao redor; e Jerusalém habitará de novo no seu lugar, em Jerusalém.
pt.B: Naquele dia farei os clãs de Judá como um braseiro posto num monte de lenha, como uma tocha acesa no meio de feixes de trigo. Eles consumirão todos os povos ao redor, à direita e à esquerda, enquanto Jerusalém permanecerá segura no seu lugar.
pt.R: Naquele dia vou fazer as famílias de Judá ficarem como uma panela de brasas num monte de lenha, ou como uma tocha acesa no meio de feixes de trigo. Elas vão destruir todas as nações ao seu redor, de todos os lados. Mas Jerusalém vai continuar segura onde está.

decisions.choice: a pot of fire among wood, a torch among sheaves: Judah will set the enemy ablaze
decisions.reason: A pot of live coals was used to carry fire; set down in a woodpile, it sets the whole pile alight. A torch among cut grain does the same (Judges 15:4-5). The small clans of Judah will consume the nations around them.

decisions.choice: on the right and on the left: on every side
decisions.reason: The phrase means in every direction (Isaiah 9:19; 54:3).

decisions.choice: Jerusalem will dwell again in her place, in Jerusalem: the city will stay where it is, unmoved
decisions.reason: The Hebrew names Jerusalem twice: the people of Jerusalem (the first time) will live on in their city (the second time). The city that the nations meant to carry off stays on its own site (14:10).

decisions.choice: firepot (B); a pot of burning coals (R); stays secure in its place (B); will stay safe where it is (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say what the "pot of fire" was (m1), and say "in its place" once, without the second "in Jerusalem" (m3).

decisions.choice: um braseiro (L, B); uma panela de brasas (R); uma tocha
decisions.reason: "Braseiro" is the Portuguese word for a pot of live coals (m1); Readable describes it.

source.text: וְהוֹשִׁ֧יעַ יְהוָ֛ה אֶת־אָהֳלֵ֥י יְהוּדָ֖ה בָּרִֽאשֹׁנָ֑ה לְמַ֨עַן לֹֽא־תִגְדַּ֜ל תִּפְאֶ֣רֶת בֵּית־דָּוִ֗יד וְתִפְאֶ֛רֶת יֹשֵׁ֥ב יְרוּשָׁלִַ֖ם עַל־יְהוּדָֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: And Yahweh will save the tents of Judah at first, so that will not be great [the] glory of [the] house of David and [the] glory of [the] inhabitant of Jerusalem over Judah.

en.L: And {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} will save the tents of Judah at first, so that the splendor of the house of David and the splendor of the inhabitants of Jerusalem may not grow great over Judah.
en.B: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} will rescue the tents of Judah first, so that the honor of the house of David and of the people of Jerusalem will not be raised above Judah.
en.R: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} will rescue the people of the towns and villages of Judah first. Then the royal family of David and the people of Jerusalem will not think they are more important than the rest of Judah.

pt.L: E {{divine_name:o SENHOR|Javé}} salvará primeiro as tendas de Judá, para que o esplendor da casa de Davi e o esplendor dos habitantes de Jerusalém não se engrandeçam sobre Judá.
pt.B: {{divine_name:O SENHOR|Javé}} livrará primeiro as tendas de Judá, para que a honra da casa de Davi e a do povo de Jerusalém não sejam exaltadas acima de Judá.
pt.R: {{divine_name:O SENHOR|Javé}} vai livrar primeiro o povo das cidades e aldeias de Judá. Assim, a família real de Davi e o povo de Jerusalém não vão pensar que são mais importantes do que o resto de Judá.

decisions.choice: the tents of Judah: the people of the countryside
decisions.reason: "Tents" is an old word for homes (1 Kings 8:66; Jeremiah 30:18). Here it means the open towns and villages of Judah, which had no walls to protect them, in contrast to the walled city of Jerusalem.

decisions.choice: so that the glory of the house of David ... may not be made great over Judah: no pride of the capital over the rest
decisions.reason: The LORD saves the weakest first, so that the royal family and the capital cannot boast over the countryside. The victory is the LORD's, shared by all his people (1 Corinthians 1:27-29 gives the same reason for God's choices).

decisions.choice: the people of the towns and villages of Judah; the royal family of David; think they are more important (R)
decisions.reason: Readable explains "the tents of Judah" (m1) and what "glory over Judah" means (m2).

source.text: בַּיּ֣וֹם הַה֗וּא יָגֵ֤ן יְהוָה֙ בְּעַד֙ יוֹשֵׁ֣ב יְרוּשָׁלִַ֔ם וְהָיָ֞ה הַנִּכְשָׁ֥ל בָּהֶ֛ם בַּיּ֥וֹם הַה֖וּא כְּדָוִ֑יד וּבֵ֤ית דָּוִיד֙ כֵּֽאלֹהִ֔ים כְּמַלְאַ֥ךְ יְהוָ֖ה לִפְנֵיהֶֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: On that day Yahweh will defend the inhabitant of Jerusalem, and will be the one stumbling among them on that day like David, and the house of David like God, like [the] angel of Yahweh before them.

en.L: In that day {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} will defend the inhabitants of Jerusalem, and the one who stumbles among them in that day will be like David; and the house of David like God, like the angel of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} before them.
en.B: On that day {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} will shield the people of Jerusalem. On that day even the feeblest of them will be like David, and David's house like God, like the angel of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} at their head.
en.R: At that time {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} will protect the people of Jerusalem. Even the weakest of them will be as strong as King David. David's family will be like God, like the angel of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} who leads them.

pt.L: Naquele dia {{divine_name:o SENHOR|Javé}} defenderá os habitantes de Jerusalém, e o que tropeça entre eles naquele dia será como Davi; e a casa de Davi, como Deus, como o anjo {{divine_name:do SENHOR|de Javé}} diante deles.
pt.B: Naquele dia {{divine_name:o SENHOR|Javé}} protegerá como um escudo o povo de Jerusalém. Naquele dia, até o mais fraco entre eles será como Davi, e a casa de Davi será como Deus, como o anjo {{divine_name:do SENHOR|de Javé}} à frente deles.
pt.R: Naquele dia {{divine_name:o SENHOR|Javé}} vai proteger o povo de Jerusalém. Até o mais fraco deles vai ser tão forte como o rei Davi. A família de Davi vai ser como Deus, como o anjo {{divine_name:do SENHOR|de Javé}} que vai à frente deles.

decisions.choice: the one who stumbles will be like David: the weakest will be as strong as the warrior king
decisions.reason: "The one who stumbles" is the weak and feeble (1 Samuel 2:4). David was remembered as the great warrior who killed Goliath and won Israel's wars. On that day even the weakest will fight like him.

decisions.choice: the house of David will be like God, like the angel of the LORD: like a divine leader going ahead of the people
decisions.reason: The word for God can also mean a divine or heavenly being, and the next words limit it: "like the angel of the LORD before them". The angel of the LORD went before Israel out of Egypt (Exodus 14:19; 23:20; 32:34). The royal house will lead the people with God's own strength. People said of David himself that he was "like the angel of God" in wisdom (2 Samuel 14:17, 20; 19:28).

decisions.choice: defend: shield
decisions.reason: The verb is the one used in 9:15, from the word for a shield.

decisions.choice: In that day ... in that day (L); On that day ... On that day (B); At that time (R, once)
decisions.reason: The formula follows the wording set in Isaiah. Readable says it once, since the second only repeats the first, and says "as strong as King David" to make the comparison clear (m1).

source.text: וְהָיָ֖ה בַּיּ֣וֹם הַה֑וּא אֲבַקֵּ֗שׁ לְהַשְׁמִיד֙ אֶת־כָּל־הַגּוֹיִ֔ם הַבָּאִ֖ים עַל־יְרוּשָׁלִָֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: And it will be on that day [that] I will seek to destroy all the nations that come against Jerusalem.

en.L: And it will be in that day [that] I will seek to wipe out all the nations that are coming against Jerusalem.
en.B: On that day I will set about destroying every nation that comes against Jerusalem.
en.R: At that time I will make sure that all the nations that attack Jerusalem are destroyed.

pt.L: E acontecerá naquele dia [que] buscarei destruir todas as nações que vêm contra Jerusalém.
pt.B: Naquele dia tratarei de destruir todas as nações que vierem contra Jerusalém.
pt.R: Naquele dia vou fazer com que sejam destruídas todas as nações que atacarem Jerusalém.

decisions.choice: I will seek to destroy: I will set myself to destroy
decisions.reason: When the LORD "seeks" to do something, it is not an attempt that might fail but a firm purpose. The nations that come against Jerusalem will be destroyed.

decisions.choice: set about (B); make sure that (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable avoid "seek to", which in English suggests an attempt that might fail (m1).

source.text: וְשָׁפַכְתִּי֩ עַל־בֵּ֨ית דָּוִ֜יד וְעַ֣ל׀יוֹשֵׁ֣ב יְרוּשָׁלִַ֗ם ר֤וּחַ חֵן֙ וְתַ֣חֲנוּנִ֔ים וְהִבִּ֥יטוּ אֵלַ֖י אֵ֣ת אֲשֶׁר־דָּקָ֑רוּ וְסָפְד֣וּ עָלָ֗יו כְּמִסְפֵּד֙ עַל־הַיָּחִ֔יד וְהָמֵ֥ר עָלָ֖יו כְּהָמֵ֥ר עַֽל־הַבְּכֽוֹר׃

records.literal_gloss: And I will pour out on [the] house of David and on [the] inhabitant of Jerusalem a spirit of grace and supplications, and they will look to me, [the one] whom they have pierced; and they will mourn over him like [the] mourning over the only [child], and [there will be] bitterness over him like [the] bitterness over the firstborn.

en.L: And I will pour out upon the house of David and on the inhabitants of Jerusalem a spirit of grace and of pleas for mercy, and they will look on {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, the one they pierced; and they will mourn for him as one mourns for an only [son], and grieve bitterly for him as one grieves bitterly for a firstborn.
en.B: On the house of David and on the people of Jerusalem I will pour out a spirit of grace and of prayer for mercy. They will look on {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, the one they pierced, and they will mourn for him as one mourns for an only son, and weep bitterly over him as for a firstborn son.
en.R: I will pour out on the family of David and the people of Jerusalem a spirit of kindness and of praying for mercy. They will look on {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, the one they pierced. They will mourn for him as parents mourn for their only son. They will cry bitterly over him as people cry over the death of their oldest son.

pt.L: E derramarei sobre a casa de Davi e sobre os habitantes de Jerusalém um espírito de graça e de súplicas, e olharão para {{deity_pronoun:mim|Mim}}, a quem traspassaram; e o prantearão como se pranteia por um [filho] único, e chorarão amargamente por ele como se chora amargamente por um primogênito.
pt.B: Sobre a casa de Davi e sobre o povo de Jerusalém derramarei um espírito de graça e de súplica. Olharão para {{deity_pronoun:mim|Mim}}, a quem traspassaram, e o prantearão como se pranteia um filho único, e chorarão amargamente por ele como por um filho primogênito.
pt.R: Vou derramar sobre a família de Davi e sobre o povo de Jerusalém um espírito de bondade e de oração pedindo misericórdia. Olharão para {{deity_pronoun:mim|Mim}}, a quem traspassaram. Vão chorar por ele como os pais choram por um filho único. Vão chorar amargamente por ele como se chora a morte do filho mais velho.

decisions.choice: a spirit of grace and of pleas for mercy: God's gift that moves the people to seek his mercy
decisions.reason: To "pour out" a spirit is God's own gift of a new heart and will (Joel 3:1; Ezekiel 39:29). "Grace" is God's favor, and the second word means pleading for mercy. The spirit God gives turns the people to him in sorrow and prayer.

decisions.choice: they will look on me: the Hebrew text, against the reading "on him"
alternatives: they will look on him, the one they pierced
decisions.reason: The standard Hebrew text, with most manuscripts, has "on me", and the Septuagint agrees. A number of medieval Hebrew manuscripts read "on him", which makes the sentence run more smoothly into "they will mourn for him". The harder reading "on me" is very likely the original, since scribes would change it to "on him" and not the other way round. It is kept here. John 19:37 quotes the verse as "they will look on the one they pierced", without either pronoun.

decisions.choice: me, the one they pierced ... him: who is pierced
alternatives: they will look to me concerning the one they pierced (a person distinct from God)
decisions.reason: The LORD speaks, and says "they will look on me"; the next words, "the one they pierced", may describe the LORD himself, and the verse then goes on to speak of "him". Three main readings are given. First, the LORD so binds himself to the one pierced that to pierce him was to strike at the LORD. Second, the words may mean "they will look to me concerning the one they pierced", so that the pierced one is a person distinct from God: some Jewish readers have seen a leader of the people killed in battle, and the Talmud speaks of a messiah son of Joseph who will be slain. Third, the New Testament reads the verse of Jesus, pierced on the cross (m6). The Hebrew allows the first two; the text does not say who the pierced one is.

decisions.choice: pierced: thrust through, killed
decisions.reason: The verb means to run someone through with a sword or spear, usually to death (Numbers 25:8; 1 Samuel 31:4). In 13:3 it is used of parents running through a son who prophesies falsely. The Septuagint read a similar verb meaning "mocked" or "danced in triumph".

decisions.choice: mourn as for an only son, as for a firstborn: the deepest grief
decisions.reason: The loss of an only son, or of the firstborn, was the bitterest grief there was, because it ended a family's future (Amos 8:10; Jeremiah 6:26). The mourning is for the one pierced, and it goes with repentance: the people grieve for what they have done.

decisions.choice: quoted in John 19:37, and taken up in Revelation 1:7
decisions.reason: John 19:37 quotes this verse when a soldier pierces the side of Jesus on the cross: "They will look on the one they pierced". Revelation 1:7 joins it to Daniel 7:13 of Jesus' coming: every eye will see him, "even those who pierced him", and all the tribes of the earth will mourn (compare verses 12-14 here).

decisions.choice: on me (deity_pronoun setting); him (no setting)
decisions.reason: "Me" is the LORD speaking of himself, so it takes the deity_pronoun setting, as every pronoun the LORD uses of himself does. "Him", the one mourned, takes none. The verse moves to the third person, and whether "him" is the LORD, a human figure, or Jesus as the New Testament reads it, is the question the decisions leave open (m3). As with the king of 9:9, a capital letter would settle it.

decisions.choice: they will look on me, the one they pierced (every level); as for an only son
decisions.reason: The words "they will look on me, the one they pierced" are the same at every level, as set for this verse, so that the reader can follow the quotation in John 19:37. The comparison with mourning for an only son follows Amos 8:10.

decisions.choice: olharão para mim, a quem traspassaram (every level)
decisions.reason: The words keep one wording at every level, as the English does (r-en-2), so that the reader can follow the quotation: "traspassar" is the verb John 19:37 and Revelation 1:7 use in Portuguese (m4, m6). The Hebrew has "para mim" (m2), so Portuguese follows it here, where John's Portuguese has "para aquele" from the Greek. "Mim" is the LORD speaking of himself and takes the deity_pronoun span; "o", "ele", the one mourned, take none (r-en-1).

decisions.choice: um espírito de graça e de súplicas (L, B); de bondade e de oração pedindo misericórdia (R)
alternatives: um espírito de favor e de rogos
decisions.reason: "Graça" and "súplica" (m1) are the Portuguese words for God's favour and pleading for mercy; Readable spells them out, as the English Readable does.

source.text: בַּיּ֣וֹם הַה֗וּא יִגְדַּ֤ל הַמִּסְפֵּד֙ בִּיר֣וּשָׁלִַ֔ם כְּמִסְפַּ֥ד הֲדַדְ־רִמּ֖וֹן בְּבִקְעַ֥ת מְגִדּֽוֹן׃

records.literal_gloss: On that day will be great the mourning in Jerusalem, like [the] mourning of Hadad-rimmon in [the] plain of Megiddo.

en.L: In that day the mourning in Jerusalem will be great, like the mourning of Hadad-rimmon in the plain of Megiddo.
en.B: On that day the mourning in Jerusalem will be as great as the mourning at Hadad-rimmon in the plain of Megiddo.
en.R: At that time the people of Jerusalem will mourn as bitterly as the people mourned at Hadad-rimmon in the valley of Megiddo.

pt.L: Naquele dia o pranto em Jerusalém será grande, como o pranto de Hadade-Rimom na planície de Megido.
pt.B: Naquele dia o pranto em Jerusalém será tão grande como o pranto em Hadade-Rimom, na planície de Megido.
pt.R: Naquele dia o povo de Jerusalém vai chorar tão amargamente como o povo chorou em Hadade-Rimom, no vale de Megido.

decisions.choice: the mourning of Hadad-rimmon in the plain of Megiddo: probably the mourning for King Josiah
alternatives: the ritual mourning for the god Hadad-rimmon
decisions.reason: Hadad-rimmon is named only here. It is most often taken as a place near Megiddo, and the mourning as the great lament for King Josiah, who was killed in battle with Pharaoh Neco in the plain of Megiddo in 609 BC (2 Kings 23:29; 2 Chronicles 35:22-25). His death was mourned for generations. Others take Hadad-rimmon as the name of a storm god, Hadad, also called Rimmon (2 Kings 5:18), whose worshipers mourned him each year as dead, as women wept for Tammuz (Ezekiel 8:14). Either way, the comparison is with a mourning remembered as the greatest the people knew.

decisions.choice: the mourning at Hadad-rimmon (B, R); valley of Megiddo (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable read Hadad-rimmon as a place (m1); Literal keeps "of", which allows either reading. Readable says "valley" as 2 Chronicles 35:22 does.

decisions.choice: Hadade-Rimom; Megido; a planície (L, B), o vale (R)
decisions.reason: The place (m1) is written as Portuguese writes its sounds, "Hadade-Rimom", with the vowel Portuguese adds and the final "m" of "Rimom"; "Megido" as 2 Chronicles 35:22 has it in Portuguese, where Readable takes "vale" from.

source.text: וְסָפְדָ֣ה הָאָ֔רֶץ מִשְׁפָּח֥וֹת מִשְׁפָּח֖וֹת לְבָ֑ד מִשְׁפַּ֨חַת בֵּית־דָּוִ֤יד לְבָד֙ וּנְשֵׁיהֶ֣ם לְבָ֔ד מִשְׁפַּ֤חַת בֵּית־נָתָן֙ לְבָ֔ד וּנְשֵׁיהֶ֖ם לְבָֽד׃

records.literal_gloss: And will mourn the land, clans [by] clans, alone; [the] clan of [the] house of David alone, and their wives alone; [the] clan of [the] house of Nathan alone, and their wives alone;

en.L: And the land will mourn, clan by clan, each by itself: the clan of the house of David by itself, and their wives by themselves; the clan of the house of Nathan by itself, and their wives by themselves;
en.B: The whole land will mourn, each clan on its own: the clan of David's house on its own, and their wives on their own; the clan of Nathan's house on its own, and their wives on their own;
en.R: Everyone in the land will mourn, each family group by itself. The family of David will mourn by themselves, and their wives by themselves. The family of Nathan will mourn by themselves, and their wives by themselves.

pt.L: E a terra pranteará, clã por clã, cada um à parte: o clã da casa de Davi à parte, e as suas mulheres à parte; o clã da casa de Natã à parte, e as suas mulheres à parte;
pt.B: A terra inteira pranteará, cada clã separadamente: o clã da casa de Davi separadamente, e as suas mulheres separadamente; o clã da casa de Natã separadamente, e as suas mulheres separadamente;
pt.R: Todas as pessoas da terra vão chorar, cada família sozinha. A família de Davi vai chorar sozinha, e as mulheres dela sozinhas. A família de Natã vai chorar sozinha, e as mulheres dela sozinhas.

decisions.choice: clan by clan, each by itself, and their wives by themselves: the whole people in mourning, family by family
decisions.reason: The mourning is not a crowd's but each family's, and the men and the women mourn apart, as was the custom at times of solemn mourning and prayer. The phrase "by itself" is repeated eleven times in verses 12-14, so that no family is left out.

decisions.choice: the house of David, the house of Nathan: the royal line and a branch of it
decisions.reason: Nathan is most likely David's son (2 Samuel 5:14), whose line is traced in Luke 3:31; it may instead be Nathan the prophet. With Levi and Shimei (verse 13), the list names two royal families and two priestly ones: the leaders mourn first.

decisions.choice: by itself (L); on its own (B); by itself, by themselves (R); comma at the end (L, B)
decisions.reason: Every level repeats the phrase as the Hebrew does. The sentence runs on to the end of verse 14, so Literal and Balanced end with a semicolon and go on; Readable makes each family a sentence. "Wives" may also be "women".

decisions.choice: à parte (L); separadamente (B); sozinha(s) (R); Natã
decisions.reason: The phrase is repeated at every level as the Hebrew repeats it (m1), as the English does (r-en-1). "Natã" is the usual Brazilian form of Nathan (m2), as 2 Samuel 5:14 has it.

source.text: מִשְׁפַּ֤חַת בֵּית־לֵוִי֙ לְבָ֔ד וּנְשֵׁיהֶ֖ם לְבָ֑ד מִשְׁפַּ֤חַת הַשִּׁמְעִי֙ לְבָ֔ד וּנְשֵׁיהֶ֖ם לְבָֽד׃

records.literal_gloss: [the] clan of [the] house of Levi alone, and their wives alone; [the] clan of the Shimeite alone, and their wives alone;

en.L: the clan of the house of Levi by itself, and their wives by themselves; the clan of the Shimeites by itself, and their wives by themselves;
en.B: the clan of Levi's house on its own, and their wives on their own; the clan of the Shimeites on its own, and their wives on their own;
en.R: The family of Levi will mourn by themselves, and their wives by themselves. The family of Shimei will mourn by themselves, and their wives by themselves.

pt.L: o clã da casa de Levi à parte, e as suas mulheres à parte; o clã dos simeítas à parte, e as suas mulheres à parte;
pt.B: o clã da casa de Levi separadamente, e as suas mulheres separadamente; o clã dos simeítas separadamente, e as suas mulheres separadamente;
pt.R: A família de Levi vai chorar sozinha, e as mulheres dela sozinhas. A família de Simei vai chorar sozinha, e as mulheres dela sozinhas.

decisions.choice: the house of Levi and the Shimeites: the priestly tribe and one of its families
decisions.reason: Levi is the priestly tribe. Shimei was a grandson of Levi, whose descendants formed one of the families of the Levites (Numbers 3:17-21). As the house of Nathan is a branch of David's house, so the Shimeites are a branch of Levi's.

decisions.choice: The family of Shimei (R)
decisions.reason: Readable says "the family of Shimei" for "the clan of the Shimeites", as it says "family" for each clan.

decisions.choice: os simeítas (L, B); a família de Simei (R)
decisions.reason: The clan (m1) is "os simeítas", from "Simei", kept apart from "os simeonitas", the tribe of Simeon; Readable says "a família de Simei", as the English Readable does.

source.text: כֹּ֗ל הַמִּשְׁפָּחוֹת֙ הַנִּשְׁאָר֔וֹת מִשְׁפָּחֹ֥ת מִשְׁפָּחֹ֖ת לְבָ֑ד וּנְשֵׁיהֶ֖ם לְבָֽד׃ס

records.literal_gloss: all the clans that are left, clans [by] clans, alone, and their wives alone.

en.L: all the clans that are left, clan by clan, each by itself, and their wives by themselves.
en.B: and all the clans that remain, each clan on its own, and their wives on their own.
en.R: All the other family groups will do the same. Each family will mourn by itself, and their wives by themselves.

pt.L: todos os clãs que restarem, clã por clã, cada um à parte, e as suas mulheres à parte.
pt.B: e todos os clãs que restarem, cada clã separadamente, e as suas mulheres separadamente.
pt.R: Todas as outras famílias vão fazer o mesmo. Cada família vai chorar sozinha, e as mulheres de cada uma sozinhas.

decisions.choice: all the clans that are left: every other family of the people
decisions.reason: The list ends by including all the rest. Not one family stays out of the mourning of verse 10.

decisions.choice: will do the same (R)
decisions.reason: Readable makes the end of the list a sentence of its own.
